findings.title: Paginated getSubGroupsStream overloads still NPE when the group is deleted concurrently
findings.body: The PR fixes getSubGroupsCount() by tolerating modelSupplier.get() returning null when the group was concurrently deleted, but the three paginated getSubGroupsStream overloads (lines 254-269: getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer), getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer), and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer)) still dereference modelSupplier.get() directly, e.g. 'return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(search, firstResult, maxResults);'. Under the exact same race this PR targets — the cached group entry was read, then another transaction deletes the group before the call — modelSupplier.get() returns null and these methods throw a NullPointerException, surfacing as an HTTP 500 on endpoints such as GET /admin/realms/{realm}/groups/{id}/children. The same null handling should be applied there (return Stream.empty() or delegate consistently).

findings.title: Concurrency test asserts before the reader thread finishes, so it can pass even if the NPE still occurs
findings.body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, the reader thread is started and never joined: the main thread deletes the groups, sets deletedAll=true, and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty. The reader thread can be in the middle of its final groups() call when the assertion executes; an exception (such as the HTTP 500 caused by the NPE this PR fixes) can be added to caughtExceptions after the assertion has already passed, so the test reports success while the regression is still present, and conversely the timing makes it flaky. The test should keep a reference to the thread, set deletedAll, join() the thread (with a timeout), and only then assert that caughtExceptions is empty.

findings.title: Reader thread spins forever if a group delete throws
findings.body: deletedAll.set(true) on line 155 is only reached if all 100 remove() calls succeed. If any delete throws, the test fails but the non-daemon reader thread keeps looping and issuing list requests against the server indefinitely (until JVM exit), consuming CPU and adding load for the remainder of the test suite run. The delete loop should be wrapped in a try/finally that sets deletedAll (and, per the other finding, joins the thread) so the background thread is always stopped.
